_about: Weather, water clarity and insect hatches. A new day draws one weather and one clarity, then builds its hatches from the list below.

weather.label: Bright sun
weather.note: High sun and sharp shadows. Fish in thin, clear water are skittish.

weather.label: Soft overcast
weather.note: Grey, even light. Trout feel safe and feed with confidence.

weather.label: Light drizzle
weather.note: Fine rain dimples the water and hides your line. Small olives love this weather.

clarity.label: Gin clear
clarity.note: You can count pebbles at two metres.

clarity.label: Slightly tinged
clarity.note: A touch of colour from rain upstream. Heavier tippet goes unnoticed.

hatches.label: Mayfly duns
hatches.signs: Medium-sized mayflies sail down the current like little sailboats. Here and there a fish takes one with a confident, splashy rise.

hatches.label: Small olives
hatches.signs: Tiny grey-olive mayflies are hatching. Soft, sipping rises dimple the slower water.

hatches.label: Hoppers & beetles
hatches.signs: Grasshoppers click in the warm grass along the banks, and now and then one lands on the water. Something takes it with a heavy slurp near the bank.

hatches.label: Evening caddis
hatches.signs: Moth-like caddis flutter and skitter over the surface. Fish slash at them, sometimes leaping clear.

hatches.label: Spinner fall
hatches.signs: Spent mayfly spinners lie flat in the film, wings glinting. Big fish sip them with almost no disturbance on the flat.

quietNotes.dawn: Mist hangs over the pool. Nothing is hatching yet. Any feeding happens near the bottom.
quietNotes.morning: The river is waking up. No insects on the surface. The trout are picking nymphs off the stones.
quietNotes.midday: Bright and still. No rises anywhere. Fish have moved into deeper or broken water, close to the bottom.
quietNotes.afternoon: A lazy afternoon. The surface is empty. Food is drifting underneath.
quietNotes.evening: The light softens and the river feels expectant, but nothing is on the water yet.
quietNotes.dusk: Bats are out over the flat. Big browns leave cover after dark to hunt.
